use_case_name: Add Files to an Existing Archive

claims.content: Allow users to add one or more files or archives to an existing archive without destroying original contents, optionally with password/keyfile protection.

goal.raw_text: Allow users to add one or more files or archives to an existing archive without destroying original contents, optionally with password/keyfile protection.

claims.content: User
An existing archive must be present in the computer system, as users are allowed to update an archive by adding extra objects to an already existing archive.
One or more objects (files or archives) must be available for selection to be added to the archive.
The user must have access to the file manager interface or equivalent input device to select objects and initiate the add operation.

User selects one or more objects to be added to an archive from file manager interface and then presses the button writing “Add” on it from the toolbar, or clicks the right button of the mouse and selects “Add” from the submenu, or selects “Add to separate archives” from “Send to” menu.

trigger.raw_text: User selects one or more objects to be added to an archive from file manager interface and then presses the button writing “Add” on it from the toolbar, or clicks the right button of the mouse and selects “Add” from the submenu, or selects “Add to separate archives” from “Send to” menu.

claims.content: User selects one or more objects (files or archives) to be added to an existing archive from the file manager interface.

User initiates the add operation by pressing the “Add” button on the toolbar, or by right-clicking and selecting “Add” from the context menu, or by selecting “Add to separate archives” from the “Send to” menu.
The system opens the Create archive window (also referred to as Create archive Interface), which is used for updating existing archives by adding objects.
In the Create archive window, the user can optionally set a password and/or keyfile for encryption (“locking”) of the updated archive.

The system adds the selected objects to the existing archive without deleting or altering the original contents; the added objects retain their content and name and are stored at the same space where they were initially located.
The system updates the archive in place — the storage space remains the same as before the update, and compression to read-only supported formats is not performed during this operation.
The user can approach the Create archive window by pressing the button writing “File” on it in file manager interface and then selecting “Create archive” from the submenu that appears.
The user can approach the Create archive window by pressing the button writing “Browser” on it in file manager interface and then selecting “Go to archiving layout” from the submenu that appears.
If the user attempts to add files to an archive format that is read-only supported, the system does not allow compression during the update operation.

If encryption (password/keyfile) is applied but the target archive format does not support it, the system may not apply locking as expected — though PeaZip supports decryption of encrypted files, encryption capability depends on format support.
The archive is updated with the selected objects added, and its storage space remains the same as before the update.
The original contents of the archive are not destroyed or deleted; they retain their content and name.
The newly added objects retain their content and name and remain saved at the same space of the computer system where they were initially stored.
If encryption was applied by the user, the updated archive is locked with the specified password and (optionally) keyfile.
